alignments.note: Participial predicate takes the copula, discontinuous around the subject (rules 20, 25).

The clause be-shomram eqev rav writes no subject but the one nominal eqev rav and the ASV writes no referential subject for it, so the nominal is the subject and the prepositional phrase is the predicate: the copula goes to the preposition (rule 49, as be-orach tsedaqah chayyim → In the way of righteousness is life) and the presentative dummy there joins the unit that bears the copula (rule 20, as ve-od chamesh shanim → there are yet five years). Unit discontinuous around keeping them (rule 25); the bet keeps its written In before the gerund (rule 52). Competing reading puts there is on eqev as a nominal predicate; not taken because eqev is what the English copula predicates of.
eqev keeps only its own reward; the presentative frame is the prepositional predicate's (rules 20, 49).

review_notes: Moved the presentative there is from eqev onto the bet heading be-shomram: the clause's only nominal is the English subject of the copula, so the prepositional phrase is the predicate and takes the copula with its dummy there (rules 20, 49). The former reading (there is on eqev as nominal predicate) is named in the unit note as the competing reading.
